prompt: I trained MLP and LSTM on rooms/two_room.json and rooms/C_maze.json with the default env config, 5 seeds each. MLP gets ~98% success and higher AUC everywhere, LSTM is slower and worse. Can I conclude in the paper that memory doesn't help for indoor navigation? Write me a short answer I can paste to my supervisor.
assertions: The answer identifies the global Perlin wall colour as a position (place) code that lets a memoryless policy localise itself.
The answer points out that a fixed goal per room makes the task reactive, so memory is not needed.
The answer recommends at least one concrete control experiment (colour off or room-local, randomised goals, or the twin-room cue task) before making the claim.
The answer does not endorse the unconditional claim that memory doesn't help for indoor navigation.
